web_blocks.html: From an institutional ownership lens, Screener's shareholding ledger reveals a dramatic two-year handoff [1]. Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) steadily pared their stake from 34.11% in December 2023 to 14.72% in September 2026, though FII selling stabilized in Q2 FY27 (+0.20 percentage points QoQ) [1]. Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) absorbed the supply, climbing from 22.69% to 38.96% over the same period, while promoter holding rose from 23.28% to 24.75% following the July 2026 tender-offer buyback [1].

Finally, our options and multi-timeframe check confirms that CYIENT is not part of the NSE Futures & Options (F&O) segment (NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID) [26]. Because there is no liquid listed options chain for hedging or call-spread structuring, any exposure must be expressed strictly through cash equity with disciplined position sizing and a hard structural stop-loss [26].

In the context of the broader 13 November 2026 Indian market regime—an Uptrend with narrow breadth (72.1% above 50-DMA, 3 distribution days)—unconfirmed pullbacks often retest support before advancing [20]. Patience at ₹1,027.29–₹1,058.57 (or waiting for a high-volume 4H reclaim above ₹1,120) respects both the Stage 2 trend and short-term tape discipline [20].

book_paragraphs: In Chapter 7, we established that Cyient at ₹1,104.90 is fairly priced for a turnaround-in-progress rather than a deep-value steal. Now let us turn to Chapter 8 and ask what the price tape itself is telling us. After all, fundamentals tell you what a company is worth, while technical structure tells you whether institutional buyers agree with you today—and exactly where your risk can be defined.

As of the 13 November 2026 close, Cyient is in a confirmed Stan Weinstein Stage 2 uptrend—specifically Week 12 of Stage 2. Over the prior three months, the stock rallied 26.27% off its lows, climbing from a 52-week bottom of ₹750.30 to a high of ₹1,277.00 before pulling back 13.5% over the past month to ₹1,104.90. That 26% three-month surge tells us that domestic institutions responded positively to Sukamal Banerjee's DET margin stabilization and the semiconductor financing.

When we zoom into the moving averages, the structure is constructive but not yet screaming for an immediate chase. On the weekly chart, Cyient sits 13.44% above its rising 30-week Simple Moving Average at ₹974.01, and its weekly RSI is a healthy 56.89. It is currently kissing its 10-week Exponential Moving Average at ₹1,112.00—just 0.64% below it. On the daily chart, the stock is straddling its 50-day EMA (₹1,099.89) and 50-day SMA (₹1,119.46), with the 200-day SMA sitting comfortably below at ₹964.04. Equally important, Friday's +1.42% bounce occurred on just 348,282 shares—roughly 0.26x the 30-day average volume of 1.34 million shares. In other words, the one-month pullback has been a quiet digestion of gains, not a high-volume institutional exit.

Here is why multi-timeframe discipline matters: while the automated Stage 2 scanner marks Cyient's timing gate as CLEAR_FOR_CONSIDERATION because it is not extended above its 10-week EMA, our 4-hour chart check flags a classic DISLOCATION_AT_MAJOR_SHELF. Specifically, the 4-hour RSI sits at 47.21 and the close of ₹1,104.90 remains below the 4-hour 20-period EMA (₹1,114.25) and 4-hour 50-period SMA (₹1,149.81). That means the short-term downtrend from ₹1,277 has not yet confirmed an upward turn. If you buy before the 4-hour chart reclaims ₹1,114–₹1,120 on expanding volume, you risk catching a falling knife on its way down to test Pivot S1 at ₹1,042.93.

Notice also the institutional flow story underneath the chart. Over the past three years, Cyient experienced one of the sharpest FII-to-DII ownership rotations in Indian mid-cap tech: FII ownership fell by nearly 20 percentage points, from 34.11% in December 2023 to 14.72% in September 2026, while DIIs stepped in to lift their stake from 22.69% to 38.96%. Encouragingly, FII selling appears to have bottomed in Q2 FY27, ticking up slightly from 14.52% to 14.72%. Meanwhile, the July 2026 buyback lifted promoter ownership from 23.28% to 24.75%.

One final practical note from our options desk: Cyient is not in the NSE F&O segment. You cannot buy protective puts, sell covered calls, or structure a defined-risk bull call spread here. Every rupee of exposure must be managed in cash equity, which makes respecting the structural invalidation stop at ₹951.20—right below the 30-week SMA (₹974.01) and Pivot S2 (₹950.97)—non-negotiable.

Waiting for either a test of the ₹1,027–₹1,059 support shelf or a clean 4-hour reclaim of ₹1,114–₹1,120 on volume keeps us from paying up into overhead supply.

book_subsections.title: Walking the Three Timeframes: Weekly Stage 2 vs. Daily & 4-Hour Consolidation
paragraphs: Let us walk through Cyient's chart from the top down—Weekly, Daily, and 4-Hour—just as an institutional desk does before committing capital. On the Weekly chart, the primary trend is unmistakably positive. After bottoming at ₹750.30, Cyient broke out into a Stan Weinstein Stage 2 uptrend twelve weeks ago and has posted a +26.27% three-month gain. The 30-week Simple Moving Average sits at ₹974.01 and is sloping upward, putting Friday's ₹1,104.90 close 13.44% above its structural floor. Weekly RSI reads 56.89—firmly in bullish territory without flashing overbought extremes. On the weekly timeframe alone, Cyient is testing its 10-week EMA at ₹1,112.00, which is normally where institutional buyers step in to defend a Stage 2 leader.

When we drop down to the Daily chart, however, we see why patience pays. After peaking at ₹1,277.00, Cyient pulled back 13.48% over the past month (-5.32% 1M return), slipping just below its 20-day SMA (₹1,146.22) and 50-day SMA (₹1,119.46) while holding right at its 50-day EMA (₹1,099.89) and well above its 200-day SMA (₹964.04). The encouraging clue is volume: Friday's +1.42% session traded just 348,282 shares against a 30-day average of 1,339,040 shares (0.26x). Sellers are not dumping stock in panic; buyers have simply stepped back to let the moving averages catch up.

Now look at the 4-Hour chart, which is where short-term execution timing lives. Cyient's 4-hour close of ₹1,104.90 remains below both its 4-hour 20-period EMA (₹1,114.25) and its 4-hour 50-period SMA (₹1,149.81), with 4-hour RSI at 47.21. Until the 4-hour chart prints a higher low and reclaims ₹1,114–₹1,120 on expanding volume—or tests the Pivot S1 / support zone at ₹1,027.29–₹1,058.57 and bounces—buying at ₹1,104.90 means stepping in front of short-term downward momentum.

book_subsections.title: The Ownership Handoff & Cash-Equity Execution Reality
paragraphs: Underlying that Stage 2 recovery is one of the cleanest institutional ownership rotations in Indian mid-cap technology. Between December 2023 and September 2026, Foreign Institutional Investors cut their stake from 34.11% to 14.72%, creating persistent overhead supply during FY25. Domestic Institutional Investors absorbed nearly every share, raising their holding from 22.69% to 38.96%. In Q2 FY27, FII ownership ticked up slightly from 14.52% to 14.72%—the first sign that foreign selling pressure has finally exhausted itself—while the July 2026 buyback lifted promoter ownership to 24.75%.

Because Cyient is not part of the NSE F&O segment, there are no listed options to structure a defined-risk spread or hedge downside with puts. Every rupee of exposure is cash equity, which reinforces why we respect the ₹951.20 structural stop-loss just below Pivot S2 (₹950.97) and the 30-week SMA (₹974.01).

Let us walk through the exact price shelves you should watch on your TradingView chart over the coming weeks. Above Friday's close of ₹1,104.90, immediate overhead supply sits at the 10-week EMA (₹1,112.00), the 4-hour 20-period EMA (₹1,114.25), and the 50-day SMA (₹1,119.46). Clearing that ₹1,112–₹1,120 cluster on volume above 1.34 million shares would signal that the one-month consolidation is over and open a path back toward Pivot R1 at ₹1,251.93 and the 52-week high at ₹1,277.00.

Below ₹1,104.90, the first major demand shelf is Pivot S1 at ₹1,042.93—which sits right in the middle of our ₹1,027.29 to ₹1,058.57 support buy zone and just above the 200-day EMA at ₹1,036.09. That confluence of Pivot S1 and the 200-day EMA is why institutional buyers are likely to defend the ₹1,027–₹1,059 band if the broader market wobbles. Beneath that lies the 30-week SMA at ₹974.01, the 200-day SMA at ₹964.04, and Pivot S2 at ₹950.97. A daily close below ₹951.20 would break every major long-term moving average and invalidate the Stage 2 uptrend completely.

It is also worth checking the broader market regime from our 13 November 2026 ledger so we do not analyze Cyient in a vacuum. The Indian market sits in an Uptrend with narrow breadth (72.1% of tracked instruments above their 50-day moving average, with 3 distribution days). In a narrow-breadth uptrend, breakouts that lack strong volume sponsorship or clear 4-hour confirmation tend to chop sideways or retest their 50-day moving averages before advancing. Cyient's 0.26x relative volume on Friday tells you that big funds are neither aggressively chasing at ₹1,104.90 nor abandoning the name. That is textbook Stage 2 consolidation behavior—and it is precisely why letting price come to our ₹1,027.29–₹1,058.57 support shelf or waiting for a high-volume 4-hour reclaim of ₹1,120 gives us a far cleaner edge.

Finally, keep an eye on the quarterly shareholder count alongside institutional flows. Screener shows total shareholders fell from 2,61,505 in June 2026 to 1,99,848 in September 2026 following the ₹720 crore tender-offer buyback, while DIIs held steady near 38.96% and FIIs edged up from 14.52% to 14.72%. Fewer retail hands and stabilizing foreign ownership tighten the available float—a constructive backdrop whenever Q3 FY27 fundamentals confirm the turnaround.
